archetype.name: Pocket Passer (timing-and-accuracy)
archetype.definition: A rhythm thrower who wins from the pocket with anticipation and ball placement in the 10-to-30-yard window rather than with his legs or raw arm, and whose efficiency rises and falls with how often his offense lets him throw there.

report.headline: Accurate as ever, but the offense wastes too many snaps behind the line
report.take:
Burrow is what he has always been: a pocket passer whose accuracy is the engine. A 5.35 CPOE (10th) and 71.4% completions (4th) fit a career where he has posted CPOE above 4.5 in three of the last four seasons. His 0.166 EPA per dropback (15th) is almost exactly his 2022 number and a touch above his 2025. He is a good-to-very-good starter running at his normal level, not a breakout and not a decline.

The split inside that average is the story. When the ball travels 10+ yards in the air he has been exceptional: 0.939 EPA on 43 intermediate throws with a 17.2 CPOE, and 1.537 EPA on 15 deep shots with four touchdowns. Underneath, the offense drags him down. The 31 throws behind the line have cost about 0.49 EPA each, and the 100 throws in the 0-9 range come out slightly negative, with all three of his interceptions. Chase Brown has drawn 28 targets at -0.392 EPA per target, while Higgins, Chase and Gesicki are all well positive. This is a design and personnel problem as much as a quarterback one. The average throw lands 1.3 yards short of the sticks in an offense that passes more over expectation than any team in the league.

The numbers flatter him in one place and undersell him in another. The deep touchdowns on 15 attempts and the 17-point intermediate CPOE will cool. His 22% pressure-to-sack rate is far below the 29-37% he has run every season, so the sack rate (4.5%, 9th) is likely to creep up behind a line that ranks 24th in hit rate allowed. The Week 2 game at Houston, with five sacks and a 19.4% bad-throw rate on 30.6% pressure, shows what happens when it does. On the other side, the 428-yard game against Jacksonville, now the third-ranked defense, came in a loss and still graded well. The last three games total roughly +36 passing EPA after two flat openers.

Going forward, expect top-12 efficiency on heavy volume, with the ceiling set by whether Cincinnati keeps feeding low-value screens. He has been worse once ahead by nine or more (-0.132 EPA), in the fourth quarter of close games (-0.179) and under center (-0.129). Those are small samples that mostly reflect conservative calls rather than a flaw in him.

strengths.title: Owns the intermediate and deep windows
strengths.body: Beyond 10 air yards he has been one of the most productive throwers anywhere, hitting receivers in rhythm with high completion rates over expectation. The skill is real; his career CPOE says so. The size of it, 1.5 EPA per deep throw on 15 attempts, will come down.

strengths.title: Accuracy holds up year to year
strengths.body: His completion rate over expected has been a constant through his career, ranking 1st in 2021, 3rd in 2024 and 10th in 2025, and he is top-10 again. That kind of trait doesn't regress the way touchdown rates do. It gives him a high floor in completions and success rate.

strengths.title: Volume baked into the scheme
strengths.body: Cincinnati passes more than situation predicts at a league-high rate, and Burrow has played every snap of every game. That volume supports yardage and fantasy output even in games where efficiency dips.

concerns.title: Screen-heavy underneath game bleeds value
concerns.body: Throws behind the line and running-back targets are actively negative, and the short area holds all three of his interceptions. Much of that is play design and Brown's results rather than Burrow's reads. Unless the mix changes, it caps his per-play efficiency below his 2024 level.

concerns.title: Sack luck likely to turn
concerns.body: His pressure-to-sack rate is well below his career norm, and the line allows QB hits at a bottom-10 rate. Expect more drive-killing sacks, like the five at Houston, as the season goes on.

concerns.title: Conservative when protecting leads
concerns.body: Efficiency goes negative when Cincinnati is ahead by nine or more and in close fourth quarters. Both splits are under 45 plays and mostly reflect play-calling. Still, it has shown up in two losses in which the Bengals were favored.

trend.note: Weeks 1-2 produced negative passing EPA, including a five-sack game at Houston. Weeks 3-5 have gone +14.7, +7.4 and +13.9, with aggressiveness climbing to 18.8% at Miami.

nextGame.headline: A Ravens secondary that bleeds deep shots meets his best area
nextGame.body:
Baltimore's defense is middling overall (19th in EPA), and its shape fits Burrow's season well. It is third-stingiest on short throws but 25th on deep ones, allowing 0.871 EPA per deep attempt. That is a strong nudge to skip the screens that have hurt Cincinnati and live in the 10+ yard range, where he has been best. Opposing WR1s have been the most efficient role against this defense (0.76 EPA per play, 31st), and the pass rush is ordinary (21st in sack rate). That should ease the protection worry. One counterweight: only four defenses have allowed fewer passing touchdowns per game to quarterbacks.

Availability tilts toward Cincinnati, with caveats. Trey Hendrickson (63% of snaps) was out after finger surgery as of Oct. 12, with a target return of Oct. 18. If he is still missing, an average rush gets thinner. On Baltimore's offense, Lamar Jackson's sprained ankle carries the same estimated return date, and center Cam Jurgens is still in concussion protocol. Without Jackson, the league's sixth-best offense loses its driver, and the Bengals are more likely to play from ahead. That is the one game state where Burrow's efficiency has sagged. Cincinnati's own injuries (Tanner Hudson at 26% of snaps, Colbie Young at 11%) barely touch him, and he comes off a bye with 14 days' rest. No line or weather is posted yet.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots vs a leaky back end
keyMatchups.body: Baltimore ranks 25th against deep passes, and Burrow has been at his best there. Even with natural cooling, this is the clearest edge on the board.

keyMatchups.title: Higgins against WR1 coverage
keyMatchups.body: Higgins leads the team in targets at 0.583 EPA each, and Baltimore has been the second-most generous defense to lead receivers. Feeding the top option is the direct path to big plays.

keyMatchups.title: Screens into a stingy short defense
keyMatchups.body: Baltimore is third-best on short throws and holds lead backs to -0.19 EPA per play. If Cincinnati keeps calling the Chase Brown screen game, those snaps will be wasted again.

nextGame.watch: How many of his first-half throws travel 10+ air yards versus behind the line: that ratio decides whether this is a 300-yard day or a grind.

restOfSeason.body:
The accuracy and the volume are sustainable. The scheme passes more than anyone, he hasn't missed a snap, and his CPOE has been top-10 in most seasons. Expect efficiency in the 0.15-0.20 EPA range, in line with 2022 and 2025. A move toward his 2024 level depends on Cincinnati trimming the screen game that is costing it roughly 15 EPA so far.

What regresses: the four deep touchdowns on 15 attempts and the 17-point intermediate CPOE will cool, trimming his 2.2 touchdowns a game. His sack rate should also rise toward his career pressure-to-sack norms behind a line that allows hits too often. The short-area interceptions, three on 100 throws, are the likeliest number to improve.
swingFactors: Pass protection holding up as his sack luck normalizes
Whether the offense shifts targets from Chase Brown screens to Higgins, Chase and Gesicki downfield
How far the deep-ball touchdown rate cools

bets.reason: Baltimore is 25th against deep passes and 31st against WR1s, with an average-at-best pass rush that may still be missing Hendrickson. Cincinnati's league-high pass rate over expected and the extra rest after the bye support volume.

His 2.2 touchdowns a game lean on four deep scores from just 15 attempts. Baltimore allows the fifth-fewest QB touchdowns per game and is third-stingiest on short throws, where red-zone passing gets compressed.

confidence.note: Five games; the career baseline is stable, but the depth splits rest on small samples and Baltimore's QB and edge rusher status is unresolved.
